summary: Excellent work on the ZYZZsat mission design report. All required elements are addressed with strong justification, verified hand calculations, and clear STK evidence. Your honest treatment of limitations is a real strength. To reach the top band, close the remaining analytical gaps: complete the X-band link budget, extend the access analysis beyond two days, and tighten reference details.
next_steps: Complete the X-band downlink link budget in Section 2.4 so the 50 Mbit/s rate and 3.5x margin are demonstrated by link closure rather than asserted.
Extend the STK access analysis beyond the two-day sample (e.g. a full repeat cycle or season) before generalising the six-passes-per-day claim in Table 5.
Refine loosely specified bibliography entries (e.g. 'Nature, news article', 'The Space Review, article 3887') with full author, title, date and URL/DOI details.

criteria.C1: Your introduction addresses all four requirements in detail: the 5 m GBR imaging mission, the bleaching-detection rationale, the single-satellite choice with cost/communications justification, and clearly named operator (AIMS) and customers. Literature references [1]-[6] support the discussion well. For full marks, deepen the user needs analysis - e.g. quantify how the 5 m resolution and revisit meet AIMS and GBRMPA monitoring requirements.
criteria.C2: A comprehensive, well-evidenced design: justified Vega C/Kourou trade (Table 2), orbit elements (Table 4), hand-verified sun-synchronous inclination, a clear no-manoeuvre argument, STK access statistics, data budget, and drag-sail EOL. Screenshots and appendix STK files support the work. The uncalculated X-band link budget and the two-day access sample are the main gaps preventing full marks; also note the Vega C flight-record caveat is handled acceptably via your fallback.
criteria.C3: Your conclusions are specific and quantitative, tracing directly to the evidence (e.g. the 600 km, 97.79 degree orbit giving consistent morning lighting), and you honestly identify four limitations with mitigation paths. This is well above generic. To reach full marks, tie each limitation to a concrete next action or design iteration step, showing how the design would be refined.
criteria.C4: The report is professionally structured with an executive summary, numbered sections, consistently labelled figures and tables, and IEEE-style citations [1]-[15] that match in-text usage. Writing is precise throughout. The barrier to full marks is reference completeness: several entries are loosely specified, so tighten them to full bibliographic standard. Otherwise, formatting and presentation are exemplary.
